- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast early spikes; correct by adding 10–30% to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model over-anticipates sharp drops; adjust downward by 15–25% for first 5–7 days.
- After a model forecast spike (e.g., >3x historical mean), true outcome often overshoots — apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 20–40% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 1.00 for 3+ days), model underestimates long-term growth; scale forecast upward by 15–25% for horizon >14 days.
- If model forecast mean is consistently below true outcome (e.g., 30d avg forecast < 0.8x true), apply “mean reversion bias” — add 0.15–0.25 to forecast for next 7 days.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model exhibits “oscillation error” — smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values before applying horizon adjustment.
